intro:
MechaHarness acceptance paths are told as **user stories**: short scenes about what a product needs to do, written for readers who understand features but not code. Each story has a human **narrative**, an **implementation** section that traces library code fulfilling the feature, and a **validation** section that describes how the story is tested. Story text lives only in fixture `story.json` files. This guide is **generated** from those fixtures.

See the Cursor skill `.cursor/skills/user-stories/SKILL.md` when adding features: edit fixtures, regenerate this page, and keep twin copies of the same story id identical.

personas.name: Nubble
personas.bio: Nubble keeps production and CI reliable. He cares about the right inference profile being loaded, cost and progress signals he can forward to billing or monitoring, and metrics that explain whether parallel work actually helped.

personas.name: Fangore
personas.bio: Fangore builds product applications on MechaHarness. He cares about deny-by-default permissions, product rules that models cannot override, durable local plans that survive crashes, loops that stop when they are not making progress, and context that never silently drops mandatory requirements.

personas.name: Taloneth
personas.bio: Taloneth owns judge contracts, adapter drift checks, and harness experiments. He cares about offline fixture batches, versioned recorded replies, honest shadow comparisons, validator qualification before promotion, research that rejects failing candidates, and decision exports that do not leak future outcomes.

running_suite:
Default CI runs **every** story offline (static fixture + cassettes) — no skips.

```bash
# CI / offline — all stories, zero skips
pytest -q tests/stories

# Full suite (unit + stories)
pytest -q

# Live — every model-using story against real reason + judge hosts
# (HTTP twins + static infer/judge walks; softens cassette-exact token counts)
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live   MECHA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1   MECHA_MODEL=qwen3-30b-thinking   MECHA_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8009   MECHA_JUDGE_MODEL=laya   MECHA_MAX_TOKENS=1024   pytest -q tests/stories

# Live OpenAI-compat only
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live MECHA_STORY_MODEL=openai_compat/qwen3-30b-thinking \
  MECHA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost

# Live System One only
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live MECHA_STORY_MODEL=systemone/laya \
  MECHA_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8009 pytest -q tests/stories -k refund_verdict

# Shorthand aliases (still dual-mode stories, not separate skipif modules)
MECHA_LIVE_OPENAI_COMPAT=1 MECHA_BASE_URL=… pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost
MECHA_LIVE_QWEN=1 MECHA_BASE_URL=… pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost
MECHA_LIVE_JUDGE=1 pytest -q tests/stories -k 'refund_verdict or systemone_cassette'
```

| `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND` | Behavior |
|-----------------------|----------|
| `static` (default) | In-process fixture + HTTP cassettes |
| `live` | Real servers; behavioral expects hard, cassette-exact token counts soft |

Live collects HTTP cassette twins **and** static stories that call `infer` / `judge` / `judge_route` (not pure policy, recipe-shape, `tool_loop`, or Anthropic-only walks). Flip `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live` with reason + judge URLs to prove cassettes are not fantasy.
models:
| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `static/fixture/v1` | Generic in-process model; model-agnostic paths |
| `openai_compat/<served-id>/v1` | Captured OpenAI-compat chat |
| `systemone/<served-id>/v1` | Captured System One judge wire |
